facts.text: Gantry is the high-level wrapper around the low-level Mill driver
The Gantry frame is signed: +X is operator-right, +Y is back and +Z is up; deck_origin puts WPos zero at the front-left-bottom deck corner
Gantry.connect opens the CNC mill through self._mill.connect and then validates the GRBL settings and checks the alarm state
Gantry.home homes the gantry with GRBL's standard homing command through Mill.home
Gantry.move_to takes absolute gantry coordinates x, y and z and an optional travel_z for the height during XY travel
Mill.move_to documents the direct move order as X, then Y, then Z, with no diagonal interpolation
execute_command writes the command and calls _wait_until_idle when the command does not start with $
_wait_until_idle blocks until the status line contains idle and raises on an error, an alarm or a timeout
Gantry.stop returns immediately in offline mode and otherwise calls Mill.stop
Mill.stop sends the real-time feed hold and verifies that the controller entered Hold; it raises when the status is not Hold
GRBL strips real-time characters out of the stream wherever they appear, and the write lock serialises only the write syscall, never a command/response cycle
Gantry.resume delegates to Mill.resume when not offline
Mill.resume writes the real-time cycle-start byte ~ to the serial controller
A HOLD pauses motion; Resume can continue the held motion, so the path must be checked before resuming
Gantry.get_coordinates returns the current gantry coordinates as a dict with x, y and z
Gantry.get_status returns the current status string with normalized coordinates
The operator UI reports position as current work coordinates; Idle means ready, Jog/Run means moving and ALARM means the controller is locked
The Working Volume is the allowed travel range of the configured machine; it cannot detect misplaced labware or loose objects
Working volume bounds are machine-specific and calibrated: use Calibration to measure the physical working volume
Homing and jogging move real hardware; before connecting, clear the deck, check the travel path and keep the E-stop within reach
CubOS can move real lab hardware; keep an E-stop reachable and start with minimal motion
Always home after connecting; homing drives each axis to its end stops to establish a known reference
After a physical crash, hit the E-stop if the gantry is still moving, then re-home; never trust WPos after a crash without re-homing first
